from_quote: The judicial power of the United States is” (by the plan of the convention) “to be vested in one Supreme Court, and in such inferior courts as the Congress may, from time to time, ordain and establish.
rationale: The paragraph quotes the opening words of this clause in quotation marks, attributing them to "the plan of the convention," and its footnote gives the place as "Article 3, sec. 1."
to_quote: The judicial Power of the United States, shall be vested in one supreme Court, and in such inferior Courts as the Congress may from time to time ordain and establish.

rationale: The footnote to the quotation in the first paragraph names its source by number as "Article 3, sec. 1."

from_quote: the power of instituting impeachments in one part of the legislative body
rationale: Names, as a "constitutional check," "the power of instituting impeachments in one part of the legislative body," the power of impeachment this clause gives the House of Representatives.

from_quote: constituting the Senate a court for the trial of impeachments
rationale: Names the power "of determining upon" impeachments in the other part of the legislature and "constituting the Senate a court for the trial of impeachments," the trial of impeachments set out in this clause.
to_quote: The Senate shall have the sole Power to try all Impeachments.

from_quote: the power of constituting inferior courts
rationale: Names "the power of constituting inferior courts," and the footnote attached to those words gives "the expressions of the Constitution" as "to constitute tribunals inferior to the supreme court," the words of this clause.

from_quote: the expressions of the Constitution are, to constitute “tribunals INFERIOR TO THE SUPREME COURT”
rationale: The footnote quotes the words of this clause, introducing them as "the expressions of the Constitution."
to_quote: To constitute Tribunals inferior to the supreme Court

rationale: Quotes in quotation marks the opening words of this clause, "to constitute tribunals," in discussing the power of constituting inferior courts. Medium because only two words are quoted.

from_quote: The Supreme Court is to be invested with original jurisdiction, only “in cases affecting ambassadors, other public ministers, and consuls, and those in which A STATE shall be a party.”
rationale: The paragraph quotes in quotation marks the words of this clause that give the Supreme Court "original jurisdiction"; the same words about ambassadors also appear in Article III, Section 2, clause 1, but the paragraph is discussing original jurisdiction.
to_quote: In all Cases affecting Ambassadors, other public Ministers and Consuls, and those in which a State shall be Party, the supreme Court shall have original Jurisdiction.

from_quote: the Supreme Court would have nothing more than an appellate jurisdiction, “with such EXCEPTIONS and under such REGULATIONS as the Congress shall make.”
rationale: The paragraph quotes in quotation marks this clause's words on appellate jurisdiction "with such exceptions and under such regulations as the Congress shall make."
to_quote: with such Exceptions, and under such Regulations as the Congress shall make

from_quote: A technical sense has been affixed to the term “appellate,”
rationale: Takes up the objection to "this appellate jurisdiction" as applied to matters of fact, putting this clause's word "appellate" in quotation marks.

from_quote: the expressions, “appellate jurisdiction, both as to law and fact,”
rationale: The paragraph quotes in quotation marks this clause's words "appellate jurisdiction, both as to law and fact."
to_quote: appellate Jurisdiction, both as to Law and Fact

from_quote: the Supreme Court shall possess appellate jurisdiction both as to law and FACT, and that this jurisdiction shall be subject to such EXCEPTIONS and regulations as the national legislature may prescribe
rationale: Speaks of "this particular provision" of the convention and restates its words on appellate jurisdiction "both as to law and FACT" subject to "such EXCEPTIONS and regulations."
to_quote: appellate Jurisdiction, both as to Law and Fact, with such Exceptions, and under such Regulations as the Congress shall make

from_quote: the Supreme Court will possess an appellate jurisdiction, both as to law and fact, in all the cases referred to them, both subject to any EXCEPTIONS and REGULATIONS
rationale: Summing up, the paragraph repeats this clause's words "appellate jurisdiction, both as to law and fact" and its "EXCEPTIONS and REGULATIONS" in capitals.
to_quote: appellate Jurisdiction, both as to Law and Fact
